parts.t: What are the seven residential neighbourhoods in Tsawwassen?

What is the difference between Freehold Tsawwassen and Tsawwassen North Leasehold?
Neighbourhoods south of 28 Avenue (English Bluff, Cliff Drive, Central, Pebble Hill, Beach Grove, Boundary Beach, and Tsawwassen Springs) are fee-simple freehold land in the City of Delta.
(Tsawwassen Shores and Tsawwassen Landing north of 28 Avenue) sits on Tsawwassen First Nation treaty land under 99-year prepaid residential leases with no provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax.

Which public and private schools serve Tsawwassen?

Tsawwassen is part of Delta School District 37 (SD37), served by South Delta Secondary School (SDSS, offering French Immersion and AP courses) and five elementary schools — Beach Grove, Cliff Drive, English Bluff (IB PYP), Pebble Hill, and South Park — plus Southpointe Academy (K–12 independent IB school).
Are basement suites and infill duplexes permitted in Tsawwassen?

How do Flood Construction Levels apply to Beach Grove and Boundary Beach?

Low-lying coastal parcels in Beach Grove and Boundary Beach sit inside the Boundary Bay floodplain protected by municipal seawalls and dikes, requiring new construction to meet City of Delta Flood Construction Level (FCL) elevations, whereas upland lots in Pebble Hill, Central, Cliff Drive, and English Bluff sit on elevated glacial till above the floodplain.
How does Tsawwassen compare with neighbouring Ladner?
Tsawwassen offers ocean beaches, elevated bluff views, and immediate proximity to BC Ferries and Point Roberts, while
offers a historic Fraser River harbour village and slightly shorter drive times to the George Massey Tunnel.
